stories.title: No-subcommand opencode2 launches the real application
stories.journey: Install and type opencode2; discover or start the daemon, select/create the current workspace and open the native TUI without a browser or prior session.
tests: Fresh HOME under PTY opens the native interactive view with no serve/session command.
A second terminal attaches to the same authenticated daemon without a second store owner.
Missing provider credentials opens in-app setup, not a stack trace or manual server instructions.
Redirected stdin/stdout takes a documented headless/error path and never hangs in raw mode.
Startup failure restores terminal state and leaves no partial daemon descriptor or child process.

stories.title: Authenticated singleton discovery, startup and recovery
stories.journey: Any local client safely discovers or starts one per-user/data-directory daemon with authenticated health/version negotiation and explicit lifecycle ownership.
tests: Twenty concurrent launches produce one daemon and one database owner.
Forged, stale, symlinked or other-user descriptors cannot redirect credentials or authorize a server.
An occupied port or reused PID never causes an unrelated process to be killed.
Version mismatch, failed migration and readiness timeout surface actionable errors without infinite retry.
Stop/restart rotates or preserves credentials by explicit policy and existing clients reconnect safely.

stories.title: One daemon-owned application service composition
stories.journey: Wire provider routing, sessions, tools, policy, persistence and events into one owned Rust/Tokio application engine shared by every client.
tests: A real API prompt invokes the provider and persists the settled assistant turn.
A provider tool request executes the registered native tool through the real policy broker.
Denied tools produce durable failure events and no process/file side effects.
Session cancellation reclaims owned tasks, tool processes and permits.
Two clients observe the same turn ID and state rather than duplicate private runtimes.

stories.title: Complete coding turn with tools, streaming and interruption
stories.journey: Submit a coding prompt, stream a response, review permission, execute a safe file edit and continue the same turn with durable results.
tests: Scripted external provider requests a real fixture file edit and sees the tool result on its next request.
Permission deny leaves the fixture file unchanged and UI renders the denial.
Interrupt during stream/tool execution reaches a stable cancelled state without leaked work.
Provider partial stream and retryable failure preserve settled history and do not replay ambiguous side effects.
Restart during a turn produces a truthful recovered/uncertain state, never a fabricated completed response.

stories.title: In-app provider setup and model selection
stories.journey: First run lets the user configure an authorized provider or local endpoint, choose a model/effort and complete a prompt without editing configuration by hand.
tests: Keyboard-only onboarding stores an authorized account in secure storage and completes a real protocol fixture turn.
Cancel OAuth/PKCE or credential entry leaves no half-authorized account.
Invalid credentials, endpoint failure and unavailable model show retry/change-provider actions.
Secrets never appear in logs, shell arguments, transcript, QR code or exported config.
Offline start uses cached settings/catalog and local models without requiring hosted login.

stories.title: Workspace and durable session workflows through the app
stories.journey: Open the current project, create/rename/archive/resume sessions, and maintain workspace-scoped history across terminal and web clients.
tests: Empty home/project creates the first usable session inside the app.
Close/reopen restores history and timestamps from the actual database.
Concurrent clients see consistent rename/archive membership changes.
A session or workspace ID from another authorized scope is rejected without leakage.
Large history is paginated and inactive workspace stores/watchers are released within measured bounds.

stories.title: Shared event replay and lifecycle recovery
stories.journey: All clients subscribe to ordered daemon state and recover after reconnect without losing durable messages or duplicating effects.
tests: Disconnect/reconnect from a cursor delivers each durable event once to the projection.
Expired cursor causes a bounded snapshot/resync instead of silently dropping history.
Ephemeral token deltas are not mistaken for durable committed messages.
Slow clients hit bounded buffers and receive resync/disconnect without blocking other sessions.
Daemon crash between commit and publish recovers consistent history and replays durable events.

stories.title: TUI, headless and web use the same execution service
stories.journey: Expose the real engine through registered versioned routes, CLI run/export commands and native TUI rather than separate reduced adapters.
tests: The same coding fixture has matching normalized transcript/tool results through all three clients.
Headless run/export are reachable installed commands with meaningful exit codes.
Capability API reports actual tool/plugin/attachment execution availability, not hardcoded success.
Malformed requests and authorization errors have consistent typed failure semantics.
Client disconnect does not accidentally abort or detach work contrary to the selected lifecycle contract.

stories.title: Service controls, shutdown and terminal restoration
stories.journey: Users can inspect/start/stop/restart the shared service; closing one UI does not unexpectedly terminate other clients or background work.
tests: Closing one of two TUIs preserves the remaining client and daemon-owned session.
SIGINT/SIGTERM and recoverable panics restore raw/alternate-screen/mouse state.
Unix suspend/resume and supported Windows console cancellation keep input usable.
Explicit service stop drains or cancels work by policy and releases locks/listeners/children.
Repeated startup/shutdown leaves no leaked FDs, watchdogs, port reservations or unbounded logs.

stories.title: Storage typed-history independent component contract tests
stories.journey: Independently author component tests against the existing Storage API seam for the DB-019 typed tool-history contract, using disposable real SQLite databases and no mocked storage replacement, while leaving DB-019 implementation and DB-020 integration dependencies unchanged. The test entrypoints target the existing begin_tool_round, append_tool_pair and bounded_history surface when present; this is an additive test registration and does not claim new API behavior or acceptance.
tests: Round-trip and ordering: create a disposable session and ordinary user messages, begin one real tool round, append multiple tool call/output pairs including Unicode and embedded-NUL payloads, reopen the database, and assert bounded_history returns all calls before outputs in logical emitted order with exact observable bytes; assert session isolation and feature-ledger persistence across reopen.

Header validation and fail-closed reads: exercise zero-output, partial-output and non-contiguous/cross-row identity fixtures through the real API or its documented typed errors, asserting invalid headers/pairs do not expose partial history and incomplete rounds fail closed; legacy unlinked tool rows remain rejected/unsupported rather than parsed as typed records.

Global provider limits: verify legal very large call IDs and names remain accepted within the approved global provider item/byte budgets, while item and byte gates fail before unbounded payload materialization; include the legacy raw-ID path and assert a meaningful bounded error/limit rather than allocation-dependent behavior, without requiring unsafe allocator instrumentation.

Immediate transaction rollback: force a real SQLite abort trigger or constraint failure in a disposable fixture during one pair append, then use an independent connection to assert the ordinary Tool message, call and output are all absent while pre-existing data is unchanged; a successful neighboring pair remains durable and no batch-wide rollback is implied.

Feature and compatibility lifecycle: verify typed data survives close/reopen and is isolated between sessions, legacy ordinary messages remain readable and unmodified, and unlinked legacy Tool rows fail closed through Storage::bounded_history. Fork-manager unsupported behavior is deferred to DB-020's sessions-bridge test and is not claimed here; use only existing workspace rusqlite/tempfile dependencies and bounded fixture sizes.

stories.title: Storage typed-history migration and legacy-schema test lane (existing API seam)
stories.journey: Author tests that prove only the additive format-1 feature-ledger migration observable through the existing public Storage open API plus raw rusqlite reads (rusqlite workspace dep and tempfile dev-dep already exist in crates/storage/Cargo.toml; no Cargo manifest edit, no new APIs, no stubs): a feature-version ledger row plus the typed-history DDL land atomically and idempotently across reopen while schema_meta keeps schema_version 1 and the v2 init contract is never applied over format 1 (docs/STORAGE.md:17-20), and legacy rows stay untouched. SQLite byte accounting uses typeof(x)='text' and length(CAST(x AS BLOB)) so multibyte UTF-8 and embedded NUL are measured exactly; no arbitrary 512-byte call-ID cap is introduced. Real typed-writer per-pair atomicity and multi-call replay ordering are NOT claimed here; they belong to the DB-022 installed-binary blackbox lane, and the frozen installed APP-012 RED journey at 2603565 (SHA-256 56334cb46e7b3e250f3e95a61aa6bb83289dd3562a7791a5a6daf2aac3134ef2, immutable) remains the parent oracle for real typed replay. Lane discipline: the compilable-RED plus freeze receipt (docs/TDD.md sections 2-4: test author writes, controller freezes, independent verifier runs) is MANDATORY prerequisite evidence recorded BEFORE the DB-019 implementation claim (cc.claim); this lane stays test-author scope, blocked until GREEN, and is never marked completed on RED.
tests: Open a disposable format-1 database through the existing public Storage open API only; assert schema_meta still records schema_version 1 and no typed-history tables or feature-ledger rows exist yet, so the lane is authored before any new API ships; the file compiles against existing public APIs only and fails at runtime for the missing behavior, never at compile time.

Concrete migration-failure fixture without mocks or simulated panics: pre-create via rusqlite a conflicting object in the disposable database (a pre-existing table occupying a future typed-history or ledger name with an incompatible column shape), then Storage::open again and assert via rusqlite that either the full ledger row plus every typed table exists or none does; the migration must fail atomically against an incompatible pre-existing object instead of silently skipping it (a plain CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS acceptance of wrong shape is a contract violation).

Idempotent reopen: two successive Storage::open calls on a migrated disposable database leave the ledger row, typed schema and the format-1 schema_version 1 marker byte-unchanged, and the v2 init scripts are never applied over format 1 (docs/STORAGE.md:17-20).

Exact byte accounting: rows holding multibyte UTF-8 and an embedded NUL are checked with length(CAST(x AS BLOB)) against the exact stored byte count, and neither a 512-byte call-ID cap nor any other invented narrower field limit rejects them.

Legacy-schema regression: pre-existing plain-text Tool inline messages, draft_attachments and message_activity rows remain readable and unmodified after reopen with a migrated handle; nothing rewrites history. If the current public API cannot observe the migration ordering meaningfully (the exact new table names and column shapes are not yet frozen), record the exact schema-design and fixture-binding decision for the integrator as the precondition for freezing this lane; never insert typed rows via raw SQL as proof of the real writer (that proof is DB-022) and never invent observability.

stories.title: Installed-binary typed-writer blackbox lane: per-pair atomic rollback and multi-call replay order
stories.journey: One new test file hosted in crates/storage (rusqlite workspace dep + serde_json + tempfile dev-dep already present; avoids any server dev-dependency prewire while still exercising the PRODUCT writer through the daemon) launches the exact external installed oc2 binary through std::process like the frozen tests/e2e/local_application.rs at 2603565: OC2_TEST_BINARY expect-provenance with fail-not-skip when the binary is missing, env_clear with synthetic HOME/OPENCODE_RK_HOME disposable root, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, bearer token read from the daemon-minted runtime/backend.json descriptor, loopback HTTP over std::TcpStream, real loopback provider fixture, current_dir disposable project. The daemon writes a file-backed SQLite database at the storage root state.db (crates/storage/src/lib.rs:113 StoragePaths::under root/state.db), which the test opens directly with rusqlite in the SAME process to install a RAISE(ABORT) SQL trigger as the fault point; no unsafe production fault API exists or is added. Atomicity is asserted PER PAIR (one tool call plus its message/typed rows in one immediate transaction), never per batch, and this feature performs no new blob writes (typed call/output live in bounded SQLite TEXT). The external binary build is a verifier-supplied runtime prerequisite, not a compile-time API: the file compiles today and its first run is intentionally RED (typed tables absent, replay assertions failing), frozen by the controller before DB-019 may be claimed (cc.claim) or edited. Mandatory compiled-RED plus freeze receipt precedes the implementation claim; this is test-author scope, blocked until GREEN, never false-completed, and RED never calls a nonexistent API just to fail to compile.
tests: Per-pair rollback direction A: with the daemon's state.db opened via rusqlite, install a RAISE(ABORT) trigger on the future typed-record insert that fires AFTER the tool message row write; run one real streamed tool call through the loopback HTTP turn API with the provider fixture emitting that call; assert via the public read/resume endpoints that the whole pair rolled back (no tool message without its typed record anywhere) and the success control (trigger removed) persists the pair; HTTP status faults propagate as asserted exact statuses, never assumed green under an always-abort trigger.

Per-pair rollback direction B: install the abort trigger on the existing messages insert for a selected tool pair instead; assert zero partial state (no typed record without its message) and, because the pair never began, the preceding successful pair is untouched; bounded request count and byte-capped captured stream output with RAII child kill in Drop.

Per-pair, not batch: two tool calls in one streamed round with the trigger armed only for the second pair; assert pair one durably retained and pair two absent as a complete pair (no orphan either direction) through the public API; the contract makes NO whole-batch rollback claim across separate pairs.

Multi-call and overflow replay: on a success run with two calls, restart the bounded child set (exactly one restart) and assert the follow-up provider request body carries calls before their outputs in exactly the order the actual serializer emitted, mirroring the frozen assert_typed_transcript pattern at 2603565; a round above MAX_CALLS_PER_ROUND=16 replays the retained batch's real call_id/name/raw arguments and the overflow notices with their real call_id, name and raw arguments, never empty-name rows; query counts are fixed and bounded (single session, two tool turns, one restart).

RED discipline and provenance: the file must panic when OC2_TEST_BINARY is unset or not an executable file (no skip, pattern local_application.rs:137-139), must fail against the current revision because the typed tables and replay order are absent (intentional compile-then-runtime RED on the real writer path, never a raw-SQL typed insert substitute), and full assertions later exercise the REAL writer through the daemon; env stays cleared with only the enumerated synthetic variables, the project and database live under one disposable root, children are killed and joined within the timeout bound.

stories.title: Storage durable typed tool-history feature migration and atomic per-pair append (format 1)
stories.journey: Additive format-1 feature-version ledger plus typed-history DDL applied atomically inside the existing format-1 bootstrap (crates/storage/src/lib.rs:688-705 keeps the schema_version 1 marker; docs/STORAGE.md:17-20 forbids v2 scripts over format 1). Before the first tool effect, after the existing step-limit decision at Executing, insert only a metadata-only per-provider-round header (round identity, session/turn message, round ordinal, expected_calls = the retained emitted batch length) and verify the initiating turn message exists, belongs to the session and has User role; header failure stops the turn before any call IDs or arguments are written and before any effect. Typed append rides the existing immediate-transaction pattern (append_message_with_reasoning, TransactionBehavior::Immediate, at 2603565): one immediate transaction persists the ordinary Tool message plus the typed call and output rows, exact call_id/name/raw arguments preserved byte-for-byte in bounded SQLite TEXT with no arbitrary truncation and no new blob writes, plus the output ACTUALLY sent under the existing truncate_tool_output policy. SQLite byte accounting uses typeof(x)='text' and length(CAST(x AS BLOB)); there is NO arbitrary 512-byte call-ID cap and UTF-8/NUL content is preserved. Overflow records retain the real call ID, name and raw arguments of the retained pre-truncation batch with the existing synthesized not-executed output; do not store empty-name overflow rows. No invented outcome enum, truncation-flag column or numeric code: outcome information is the existing serialized contract value stored verbatim. Records carry round/pair identity and ordering sufficient to replay all calls before their outputs for multi-call batches exactly as the serializer emitted them; atomicity is per pair (one Tool message plus its typed rows in one immediate transaction), explicitly NOT across a multi-call batch. Bounded replay reads metadata first (fixed page/keyset reads, checked arithmetic, EXISTS/LIMIT 1 for incomplete detection), never allocates from untrusted expected_calls, never uses it as an unbounded LIMIT, and never materializes payload before budget checks; legacy blob messages use a bounded read of remaining budget + 1 verified against metadata, never the unbounded BlobStore::get (storage/src/lib.rs:770-779). Incomplete rounds, including a header with zero outputs, fail closed; a pair failure cannot undo an already-executed batch and triggers no automatic replay. Deadlock note: DB-021/DB-022 stay unregistered as dependency edges because the ready-rule requires completed claims and implementation must not wait on test GREEN; the controller workflow enforces the mandatory compiled-RED plus freeze receipts of both lanes as prerequisite checkpoint evidence BEFORE this task may be claimed (cc.claim) or any product file edited; until then no implementation claim/edit and no completed claim are legal. No cycle.
tests: Storage open against a fresh and an existing format-1 database keeps the schema_version 1 marker and v2 init contract intact; the feature-ledger row and typed-history DDL land in one atomic migration step, fail atomically against a pre-existing incompatible object of the same name, and are idempotent across reopen.

Header before effects: after the step-limit decision and before the first tool effect exactly one metadata-only round header is written with expected_calls equal to the retained emitted batch length; a header failure (unknown turn message, wrong session, non-User role) leaves no header and performs no call dispatch or provider request.

Per-pair atomic append: one immediate transaction writes the existing Tool message row and its typed records together; any mid-transaction failure (unknown message_id FK violation, oversized payload, injected constraint failure) rolls the entire PAIR back with no orphaned message-without-typed or typed-without-message state observable from a second connection and original message bytes intact; a second pair in the same round is a separate transaction with no cross-pair batch rollback claim; once a pair failure is observed, no further provider request or dispatch occurs for the turn and no side effect is replayed.

Exact bounded TEXT payload: reloaded call_id, name and raw arguments equal the input byte-for-byte including multibyte UTF-8 and embedded NUL, with byte length verified via length(CAST(x AS BLOB)) and no arbitrary 512-byte call-ID cap; the stored output is the payload actually sent under the existing truncate_tool_output policy; no typed row is written to a blob. Overflow rows keep the real call ID, name and raw arguments with the existing not-executed output, never an empty name.

Bounded metadata-first replay and fail-closed: several calls and outputs in one round reload with all calls before their outputs in emitted order; paging uses fixed keyset reads, never allocates from declared expected_calls and never materializes payload before budget checks; it respects the approved provider limits (MAX_RESPONSES_INPUT_MESSAGES=100, MAX_RESPONSES_INPUT_BYTES=512*1024) without rejecting a turn before effects solely because reconstructed prior history exceeds them; a round whose header is missing outputs (including zero outputs) fails closed; legacy blob history replays through a bounded reader, never unbounded BlobStore::get.

stories.title: Sessions typed tool-record bridge (format-1 scope only)
stories.journey: Expose the typed tool-history operations through the existing SessionService ownership of Arc<Storage> (crates/sessions/src/lib.rs:331-335) using the run_blocking append pattern (crates/sessions/src/lib.rs:451-474), for the format-1 storage path only: begin_tool_round(header), append_tool_pair(round_id, pair_index, message, call, output) returning the MessageRecord, and bounded_history(session_id, limits) returning ordered HistoryItem values. Replay is metadata-first and bounded: no allocation from untrusted expected_calls, no unbounded LIMIT, no payload materialization before budget checks, and incomplete rounds fail closed. Fork sessions served by the separate SessionManager branch use a different connection; typed history on that branch returns an explicit unsupported/deferred error, never falls back to display text, never silently loses data and never implies cross-database atomicity.
tests: The bridge appends and replays typed records via the existing Arc<Storage> and run_blocking pattern; the bridge itself opens no connection and duplicates no storage ownership.

The format-1 path preserves call/output order, returns the MessageRecord plus typed receipt unchanged and bounded_history returns all calls before their outputs in emitted order, relying on the DB-019 per-pair transaction (no additional or weaker atomicity is promised here).
A typed operation requested for a fork-manager session returns an explicit unsupported/deferred error; no silent fallback to untyped text, no silent loss, no cross-database atomicity claimed.

Malformed pairings (an output without a preceding call, a message_id not owned by the session, a role mismatch, a duplicate (round_id,pair_index,kind)) map to SessionError::Contract with zero persisted state; bounded_history on an incomplete or zero-output round fails closed.

Existing append_text and append_assistant_with_reasoning behavior is byte-identical (regression); concurrency serializes only inside the SQLite immediate transaction with no unbounded queue and no lock held outside it.

stories.title: Server persisted typed Responses tool call and output replay
stories.journey: At Executing, after the existing step-limit decision and before the first tool effect, persist the metadata-only round header through the DB-020 bridge; then persist matched ResponsesItem tool call/output pairs through the bridge instead of the formatted display text at crates/server/src/lib.rs:1316-1330, and reconstruct them on resume via bounded_history while keeping the fail-closed rejection of legacy unlinked Tool entries at crates/server/src/lib.rs:1439-1457. Overflow records keep the real call ID, name and raw arguments of the retained pre-truncation batch with the existing synthesized not-executed output. Do not add any new pre-effect rejection of a turn solely because reconstructed prior history exceeds the provider follow-up request limits of 100 items or 512 KiB (crates/providers/src/responses.rs:14-16): reconstruction may still return the existing TooManyMessages/InputTooLarge errors and success of that later request is not promised. If a pair or header persistence fails after an effect already executed, the turn ends with an error event, makes no durable claim about whether the side effect occurred, offers no recoverability guarantee, performs no automatic replay and must not dispatch a further provider request or tool batch once the failure is observed; a crash before header persistence leaves no durable evidence that the round happened. Full pre-dispatch intent recording and uncertain recovery are a separate, explicitly open concern that this task does not resolve or promise.
tests: After tool execution the server persists the typed call and the output ACTUALLY sent through the DB-020 bridge instead of the formatted bracket display text (crates/server/src/lib.rs:1316-1330); exact call_id, name and raw arguments are preserved byte-for-byte.

On session resume bounded_history reconstructs ResponsesItem FunctionCall and FunctionCallOutput pairs matched by call_id in storage order, all calls before their outputs, identical to what the serializer sent, so the provider request carries same-turn tool calls and their real outputs (repairs the frozen APP-012 restart rejection at crates/server/src/lib.rs:1439-1457).

Legacy unlinked Tool rows (display text predating the repair) keep failing closed with a bad request; the server never parses display text and never silently skips entries; incomplete rounds (a header with zero or missing outputs) fail closed.

Overflow identity: a round above MAX_CALLS_PER_ROUND=16 persists and replays the retained batch's real identities and the overflow notices with their real call_id/name/raw arguments, never empty-name rows.

Pair/header failure after a side effect ends the turn with an error event, no durable occurrence claim, no recoverability guarantee and no automatic replay; once failure is observed no further provider request or dispatch occurs; no new pre-effect rejection based on the 100-item/512 KiB follow-up request limits is introduced. The installed golden journey tests/e2e/local_application.rs at 2603565 (frozen, SHA-256 56334cb46e7b3e250f3e95a61aa6bb83289dd3562a7791a5a6daf2aac3134ef2, zero test edits) transitions restart and resume from the observed 400 to the expected 201 with typed same-turn and future replay on the exact integrated revision.

stories.title: Native interactive PTY RED and frozen contract
stories.journey: Author a real stdlib PTY RED against the published line-loop binary: prove the missing native interactive contract without banners or mocks, with bounded process cleanup and terminal restoration assertions.
